headline: Clean: Platinum Rewards pays the highest cash back (10%), and its $200 fee drops to an effective $50 through the documented $150 rebate at her $50k/month spend, which fits her $100/year limit.
solution_check: Platinum earns 10.0% (doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_002: 'You earn 10.0% cash back on all eligible purchases'), more than Diamond Elite at 5% (invitation-only, $495 fee), Gold at 2.5% (requires Rho-Bank+, which she lacks), and Crypto-Cash Back at 2%. Platinum's $200 fee (platinum_001) less the '$150.00 rebate ... monthly spend threshold of $7500.00' (platinum_007) is $50/year, within her $100 cap given her $50,000/month spend. The first-year waiver promo (platinum_009) ran '2024-06-01' to '2024-12-31' and has expired by the fixed clock (2025-11-14), so it cannot block the rebate in year one (platinum_010). This matches gold[0] (Platinum Rewards Card, Sera Chen, 250000, false).
prior_note: Prior verdict was None. v1.0.1 fixed the platinum_002 title ('Earning 4% Cash Back' -> 'Earning 10% Cash Back'), which removes a contradiction that could have steered agents away from Platinum, so the task is if anything cleaner now.
notes: Leaving rho_bank_subscription out stores False, which equals the gold, so this flag cannot cause a failure here. The agent has to ask about monthly spend to justify the rebate ('DO NOT bring this up unless asked'). Even without that question, Platinum is still the highest-cash-back card she can get.
